genesis.38.p1.b1.text: About that time, Judah left his brothers and settled near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite.

genesis.38.p1.b2.text: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua, and he took her as a wife …

genesis.38.p1.b3.text: So she conceived and gave birth to a son, and Judah named him Er. Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan. Then she gave birth to another son and named him Shelah; …

genesis.38.p2.b1.text: Now Judah acquired a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

genesis.38.p2.b2.text: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; so the LORD put him to death.

genesis.38.p2.b3.text: What he did was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put Onan to death as well.

genesis.38.p2.b4.text: He may die too, like his brothers.

genesis.38.p2.b5.text: Live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.

genesis.38.p3.b1.text: After a long time Judah’s wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had finished mourning, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah.

genesis.38.p3.b2.text: Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep

genesis.38.p3.b3.text: … covered her face with a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah.

genesis.38.p3.b4.text: When Judah saw her, … she had covered her face.

genesis.38.p4.b1.text: Not realizing that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her …

genesis.38.p4.b3.text: I will send you a young goat from my flock

genesis.38.p4.b4.text: Only if you leave me something as a pledge until you send it.

genesis.38.p4.b5.text: Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.

genesis.38.p4.b6.text: Then Tamar got up and departed. And she removed her veil and put on her widow’s garments again.

genesis.38.p5.b1.text: Now when Judah sent his friend Hirah the Adullamite with the young goat to collect the items he had left with the woman, he could not find her.

genesis.38.p5.b2.text: Where is the shrine prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim?

genesis.38.p5.b3.text: No shrine prostitute has been here

genesis.38.p5.b4.text: I could not find her, and furthermore, the men of that place said, ‘No shrine prostitute has been here.’

genesis.38.p5.b5.text: Let her keep the items … Otherwise we will become a laughingstock.

genesis.38.p6.b2.text: Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she is pregnant.

genesis.38.p6.b3.text: Bring her out! … Let her be burned to death!

genesis.38.p6.b4.text: I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong.

genesis.38.p6.b5.text: Please examine them. Whose seal and cord and staff are these?

genesis.38.p6.b6.text: She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.

genesis.38.p6.b7.text: And he did not have relations with her again.

genesis.38.p7.b1.text: When the time came for Tamar to give birth, there were twins in her womb.

genesis.38.p7.b5.text: Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist, and he was named Zerah.
